report.source_text: Laboratory testing revealed elevated BUN (25.9 mg/dL) and serum creatinine (1.36 mg/dL). Her estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) was 38 mL/min/1.73 m2, as calculated using the CKD-EPI equation. Urinalysis revealed proteinuria 3 + in dipstick and microscopic hematuria (urine RBC 10–20/HPF). The spot urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (PCR) was 3.99 g/g, and 24-hour urine collection showed urine total protein of 3629 mg/day.

report.source_text: The glomerulus exhibited mesangial expansion and lobular accentuation without mesangial hypercellularity upon PAS staining (Fig. 1A), the glomerular diameter was 247.3 micrometer (Fig. 1B). The mesangial expansion is negative staining in Periodic Acid Methenamine Silver (PAM) staining (Fig. 1C). Congo-red staining was negative for amyloid (Fig. 1D). Immunohistochemistry for fibronectin (A235, DAKO) showed strong positive staining in the glomerulus (Fig. 1E). Immunofluorescence results for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen were all negative in glomeruli and vessels. Electron microscopy revealed massive mesangial and subendothelial electron dense deposits, along with diffuse foot process effacement (Fig. 1F). These deposits exhibited a granular and fibrillary substructure, with fibril diameters ranging from 11 to 16 nm (Fig. 1G).

report.source_text: Results were negative in tests for anti-nuclear antibodies (ANA), anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA), anti-glomerular basement membrane (anti-GBM) antibodies, anti-streptolysin O (ASO) antibodies, and rheumatoid factor (RF). Serologic test results were within normal limits—including IgA of 223 mg/dL (reference range, 70–400 mg/dL), IgG 844 mg/dL (reference range, 700-1,600 mg/dL), IgM 73 mg/dL (reference range, 40–230 mg/dL), C3 92 mg/dL (reference range, 90–180 mg/dL), and C4 26.9 mg/dL (reference range, 10–40 mg/dL). Negative results were obtained from serologic tests for hepatitis B, hepatitis C, and human immunodeficiency viruses. Serum M protein was not detected and serum protein electrophoresis was unremarkable.

report.source_text: The patient’s anti-hypertensive medication was changed to angiotensin II receptor blocker (Azilsartan® 20 mg/day), and torsemide (10 mg/day) was added for edema control. At 6 months after kidney biopsy, serum creatinine was 1.41 mg/dL (eGFR 36 mL/min/1.73 m2) and spot urine PCR was 2.35 g/g. At 1 year after biopsy, serum creatinine was 1.43 mg/dL (eGFR 35 mL/min/1.73 m2) and spot urine PCR was 0.48 g/g. At 2 years after renal biopsy, the patient’s renal function maintained stable (serum Cr 1.56 mg/dL, eGFR 32 mL/min/1.73 m2) and proteinuria was reduced (spot urine PCR 0.14 g/g).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 75-year-old Korean female with hypertension presented with 2 months of generalized edema and was found to have nephrotic-range proteinuria (24-hour urine protein 3629 mg/day, spot PCR 3.99 g/g) and renal insufficiency (serum creatinine 1.36 mg/dL, eGFR 38 mL/min/1.73m2) with microscopic hematuria. Extensive serologic workup was negative for secondary causes including autoimmune diseases (ANA, ANCA, anti-GBM, RF), infections (hepatitis B, C, HIV), and monoclonal gammopathy (normal SPEP, no M protein). Kidney biopsy revealed mesangial expansion with lobular accentuation, Congo-red negative staining (excluding amyloidosis), pauci-immune immunofluorescence (negative IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, fibrinogen), strong positive fibronectin immunohistochemistry, and electron microscopy showing mesangial/subendothelial electron dense deposits with granular and fibrillary substructure (fibril diameter 11-16 nm). The patient was treated conservatively with angiotensin II receptor blocker (Azilsartan) and torsemide. Over 2 years of follow-up, renal function remained stable (eGFR 38→32 mL/min/1.73m2) with marked reduction in proteinuria (PCR 3.99→0.14 g/g).

Strong positive fibronectin immunohistochemistry (A235, DAKO) on glomeruli
Pauci-immune immunofluorescence (negative IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, fibrinogen)
Electron microscopy demonstrating mesangial and subendothelial fibrillary deposits with 11-16 nm fibril diameter
Stable renal function with proteinuria reduction over 2 years on conservative therapy (ARB + diuretic)

Genetic testing for FN1 mutation (definitive confirmation of hereditary FNG)
Anti-PLA2R antibody status (not explicitly reported, though pauci-immune IF makes membranous nephropathy unlikely)
